summary: The Kohen Gadol reads from the Torah about Yom Kippur, says one part by heart, and then says eight brachos.

chunks.en: The Kohen Gadol came to read.
chunks.explain: He reads the parts of the Torah about Yom Kippur.
chunks.st: The High Priest came to read the Torah.

chunks.en: If he wanted to read in the linen clothes,
chunks.st: If he wished to read the Torah while still dressed in the fine linen garments, i.e., the priestly vestments he wore during the previous service,

chunks.en: he reads. And if not,
chunks.st: he may read wearing them; and if not

chunks.en: he reads in a white robe of his own.
chunks.st: he is permitted to read in a white robe of his own, which is not a priestly vestment.

chunks.en: The chazzan of the shul takes a Sefer Torah
chunks.st: The synagogue attendant takes a Torah scroll

words.note: The man who takes care of the shul.

chunks.en: and gives it to the head of the shul,
chunks.st: and gives it to the head of the synagogue that stood on the Temple Mount;

chunks.en: and the head of the shul gives it to the Segan,
chunks.st: and the head of the synagogue gives it to the deputy High Priest,

chunks.en: and the Segan gives it to the Kohen Gadol,
chunks.st: and the Deputy gives it to the High Priest,

chunks.he: וְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל עוֹמֵד וּמְקַבֵּל וְקוֹרֵא עוֹמֵד,
chunks.en: and the Kohen Gadol stands and takes it, and reads standing,
chunks.st: and the High Priest stands and receives the scroll from his hands.

chunks.en: and he reads "Acharei Mos" and "Ach Be'asor."
chunks.explain: These are the two parts in Vayikra about Yom Kippur.
chunks.st: And he reads from the scroll the Torah portion beginning with the verse: “After the death” (Leviticus 16:1) and the portion beginning with the verse: “But on the tenth” (Leviticus 23:26),

chunks.en: And he rolls up the Sefer Torah and holds it close to him,
chunks.st: and furls the Torah scroll and places it on his bosom

chunks.he: וְאוֹמֵר, יוֹתֵר מִמַּה שֶּׁקָּרָאתִי לִפְנֵיכֶם כָּתוּב כָּאן,
chunks.en: and says, "More than what I read before you is written here."
chunks.st: and says: More than what I have read before you is written here.

chunks.he: וּבֶעָשׂוֹר שֶׁבְּחֻמַּשׁ הַפְּקוּדִים קוֹרֵא עַל פֶּה,
chunks.en: And "Uve'asor" in Sefer Bamidbar he reads by heart,
chunks.explain: It is too far to roll to quickly, so he says it from memory.
chunks.st: The Torah portion beginning with the verse: “And on the tenth,” from the book of Numbers (29:7), he then reads by heart.
chunks.basisNote: Bartenura explains why he says it by heart.

words.en: that is in the Chumash of

words.note: Sefer Bamidbar, the book of the countings.

chunks.en: And he says eight brachos after it:
chunks.st: And he recites after the reading the following eight blessings:

chunks.en: on the Torah,
chunks.st: Concerning the Torah: Who has given us the Torah of truth;

chunks.en: and on the avodah,
chunks.st: and concerning the Temple service: Find favor in Your people Israel and accept the service in Your most holy House... for You alone do we serve with reverence;

words.note: The service in the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: and on thanking Hashem,
chunks.st: and concerning thanksgiving: We give thanks to You;

chunks.en: and on forgiving sins,
chunks.st: and concerning pardon of iniquity: Pardon our iniquities on this Yom Kippur;

chunks.en: and on the Beis HaMikdash by itself,
chunks.st: and concerning the Temple in and of itself, which concludes: Blessed…Who chose the Temple;

chunks.en: and on Yisrael by itself,
chunks.st: and concerning the Jewish People in and of itself, which concludes: Blessed…Who chose Israel;

chunks.en: and on Yerushalayim by itself,
chunks.st: and concerning Jerusalem in and of itself, which concludes: Blessed…Who chose Jerusalem;

chunks.en: and on the Kohanim by themselves,
chunks.st: and concerning the priests in and of themselves, which concludes: Blessed…Who chose the priests;

chunks.en: and on the rest of the tefillah.
chunks.st: and concerning the rest of the prayer, which concludes: Blessed…Who listens to prayer.

summary: A person who watches the Kohen Gadol reading cannot also see the bull and goat being burned, because they happen at the same time far apart.

chunks.en: One who sees the Kohen Gadol while he reads
chunks.st: One who sees the High Priest reading the Torah

chunks.en: does not see the bull and goat that are burned.
chunks.st: does not see the bull and goat that are burned;

chunks.en: And one who sees the bull and goat that are burned
chunks.st: and one who sees the bull and goat that are burned

chunks.he: אֵינוֹ רוֹאֶה כֹהֵן גָּדוֹל כְּשֶׁהוּא קוֹרֵא.
chunks.en: does not see the Kohen Gadol while he reads.
chunks.st: does not see the High Priest reading the Torah.

chunks.en: And not because he is not allowed,
chunks.st: The Mishna explains: And this is not due to the fact that one is not permitted to see both,

chunks.en: but because it was a long way between them,
chunks.st: but because there was a distant path between them,

chunks.en: and both of them are done at the same time.
chunks.st: and the performance of both of them is undertaken simultaneously.

summary: After reading, the Kohen Gadol toivels and puts on his golden clothes. Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Akiva argue when the other korbanos of the day are brought.

chunks.en: If he reads in the linen clothes,
chunks.st: If the High Priest read the Torah in sacred white fine linen garments,

chunks.en: he washed his hands and his feet,
chunks.st: he then sanctified his hands and feet as he did each time before removing the priestly vestments.

chunks.en: took off his clothes, went down and toiveled,
chunks.st: He then removed the linen garments, descended to the ritual bath, and immersed.

chunks.en: came up and dried himself.
chunks.st: Afterward he ascended and dried himself with a towel,

chunks.en: They brought him the golden clothes,
chunks.st: and they brought him the golden garments of the High Priesthood,

chunks.en: and he put them on, and washed his hands and his feet.
chunks.st: and he dressed in them and sanctified his hands and feet.
chunks.stMore: The mishna addresses those offerings whose sacrifice has still not been mentioned. The verses in Leviticus, chapter 16, detail the special offerings of the atonement service of Yom Kippur. Of those offerings, the ram of the High Priest and the ram of the people have still not been addressed. In addition to this, the additional offerings of Yom Kippur detailed in Numbers, chapter 29, have not yet been discussed. These include seven one-year-old lambs and a bull to be brought as a burnt-offering and a goat to be brought as a sin-offering.

chunks.en: And he went out and brought his ram
chunks.st: The mishna continues: He emerged and offered his ram

chunks.en: and the ram of the people,
chunks.st: and the ram of the people

chunks.he: וְאֶת שִׁבְעַת כְּבָשִׂים תְּמִימִים בְּנֵי שָׁנָה,
chunks.en: and the seven perfect lambs, a year old.
chunks.st: and the seven unblemished year-old lambs mandated to be offered that day.

chunks.en: These are the words of Rabbi Eliezer.
chunks.st: This is the statement of Rabbi Eliezer.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva says: Those offerings were not sacrificed at this point;

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.he: עִם תָּמִיד שֶׁל שַׁחַר הָיוּ קְרֵבִין,
chunks.en: they were brought with the morning tamid,
chunks.st: rather, they were sacrificed with the daily morning offering;

chunks.he: וּפַר הָעוֹלָה וְשָׂעִיר הַנַּעֲשֶׂה בַחוּץ הָיוּ
chunks.en: and the bull of the olah and the goat that is done outside
chunks.st: and the bull of the Yom Kippur burnt-offering; and the goat whose services are performed outside of the Sanctuary, i.e., in the Temple courtyard,

words.note: A korban that is burned completely on the mizbeach.

chunks.he: קְרֵבִין עִם תָּמִיד שֶׁל בֵּין הָעַרְבָּיִם:
chunks.en: were brought with the afternoon tamid.
chunks.st: were sacrificed with the daily afternoon offering.

summary: The Kohen Gadol changes his clothes again to take the ketores pan out of the Kodesh HaKodashim, and then to do the afternoon service. At the end he goes home and makes a party for his friends.

chunks.en: He washed his hands and his feet,
chunks.st: he sanctified his hands and feet

chunks.en: and took off his clothes, went down, toiveled, came up and dried himself.
chunks.st: and removed the golden garments, and he descended into the ritual bath and immersed and ascended and dried himself.

chunks.en: They brought him the white clothes,
chunks.st: They brought him the white garments again,

chunks.en: and he put them on, and washed his hands and his feet.
chunks.st: and he dressed in them and sanctified his hands and feet.

chunks.he: נִכְנַס לְהוֹצִיא אֶת הַכַּף וְאֶת הַמַּחְתָּה.
chunks.en: He went in to take out the spoon and the fire-pan.
chunks.st: Afterward he entered the Holy of Holies to take out the incense spoon and the coal pan,
chunks.stMore: which he had brought there earlier.

chunks.en: He washed his hands and his feet,
chunks.st: He again sanctified his hands and feet

chunks.en: and took off his clothes, went down and toiveled,
chunks.st: and removed the white garments and descended to the ritual bath and immersed

chunks.en: came up and dried himself.
chunks.st: and ascended and dried himself with a towel.

chunks.en: They brought him the golden clothes and he put them on,
chunks.st: They brought him the golden garments, and he dressed in them

chunks.en: and he washed his hands and his feet,
chunks.st: and sanctified his hands and feet

chunks.he: וְנִכְנַס לְהַקְטִיר קְטֹרֶת שֶׁל בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם
chunks.en: and went in to burn the afternoon ketores
chunks.st: and entered the Sanctuary to burn the afternoon incense

chunks.en: and to clean the lamps.
chunks.st: and to remove the ashes from the lamps,
chunks.stMore: which signified the end of the day’s service.

chunks.en: And he washed his hands and his feet, and took off his clothes.
chunks.st: And he sanctified his hands and feet and removed the golden garments, and he descended to the ritual bath and immersed and ascended and dried himself.

chunks.en: They brought him his own clothes, and he put them on.
chunks.st: They then brought him his own clothing and he dressed, since the service was complete and Yom Kippur was over;

chunks.en: And they walk with him to his house.
chunks.explain: They do this to give him honor.
chunks.st: and the people escort him to his house in deference to him.

chunks.en: And he would make a Yom Tov for the people who love him
chunks.st: And the High Priest would make a feast for his loved ones and his friends

chunks.en: when he came out safely from the Kodesh.
chunks.st: when he emerged in peace from the Sanctuary.

summary: A regular Kohen wears four special clothes, and the Kohen Gadol wears eight. Dressed in all eight, he may ask questions of the Urim VeTumim, but only for the king, the beis din, or the needs of the community.

chunks.en: The Kohen Gadol serves in eight garments,
chunks.st: the High Priest serves in eight garments,

chunks.en: and a regular Kohen in four:
chunks.st: and the common priest serves in four:

chunks.en: a shirt, pants, a hat and a belt.
chunks.st: In a tunic and trousers and a mitre and a belt.

chunks.en: The Kohen Gadol adds on top of these:
chunks.st: The High Priest adds another four garments beyond those worn by the common priest:

chunks.en: the Choshen, the Eiphod, the Me'il and the Tzitz.
chunks.explain: The Choshen is the breastplate with twelve stones, and the Tzitz is a gold plate on his forehead.
chunks.st: A breastplate, and an ephod, and a robe, and a frontplate.

chunks.en: In these they ask questions with the Urim VeTumim.
chunks.st: When dressed in these eight garments, the High Priest may be consulted for the decision of the Urim VeTummim.

words.note: The Urim VeTumim was a holy name of Hashem in the Choshen that helped answer questions.

chunks.en: And they only ask for the king,
chunks.st: And he may be consulted for the decision of the Urim VeTummim only on behalf of the king,

chunks.he: וּלְבֵית דִּין וּלְמִי שֶׁהַצִּבּוּר צָרִיךְ בּוֹ:
chunks.en: and for the beis din, and for someone the community needs.
chunks.st: or on behalf of the president of the court, or on behalf of one whom the community needs.
chunks.stMore: Individual inquiries are not posed to the Urim VeTummim.
